messages:
jessica: flagging a regression: short streaming chat requests (<10 tokens) have 95p latency up ~45ms after yesterday's kernel-picker rollout. Noticed host CPU up on preparse.

lin: thanks. any traces / flamegraphs? which path is hot?

jessica: attached a small pprof sample from canary hosts: most samples in tokenizer::fast_path and socket_writev + http2::window_update. kvcache still showing high hit-rate so not the main culprit.

jessica: ```
(pprof) top
24.1%  tokenizer::fast_path
19.0%  socket_writev
11.4%  http2::window_update
9.8%   parse::frame_unmarshal
7.2%   grpc::flush
6.0%   kvcache::lookup
...
```

omar: http2 window_update spikes + writev implies we're doing lots of tiny frame writes that force immediate window updates/flushes. Could be grpc flush semantics or smaller MTU combining with HPACK.

kai: the kernel-picker change pulled in kernel-vec-v2 for paperclip models. That kernel assumes chunked IO and currently disables the proxy coalesce optimization (we had a guard: if kernel.supports_vec_io then coalesce=false).

lin: so kernel selection indirectly flipped coalescing off. nasty. The new mini-batch scheduler also increased prefork to 6 threads from 3 which might saturate tokenizer thread-pool and cause more context switches.

jessica: yep. on the canary we observed many short lived syscalls: writev of ~80-200 bytes per request and a following window_update syscall. Syscall rate went up ~2.8x.

omar: mitigation ideas: 1) re-enable coalesce for vec kernels (fix kernel manifest) 2) add local write-buffering in proxy to aggregate frames up to 1KB before writev 3) route <=8 token requests through minidecode fast path 4) reduce preparse prefork concurrency to 2-3 threads.

kai: agree. also consider softening kernel-picker rules so vec kernels are only selected for >128 token shapes. We can add a simple heuristic in picker: prefer kernel variant by median_io_size.

lin: we should collect metrics first: preparse.writev_count, preparse.write_size_hist, http2.window_update_count, tokenizer.pool_wait_ms, kvcache.hit_ratio_by_shard. Maria (not on thread) had a dashboard we can reuse.

jessica: i'll add metrics and a short-lived trace config for the canary group. Also will open a tiny patch to kernel manifests to re-enable coalesce flag and add a comment.

omar: testing locally, a small patch that buffers writes until either 1KB or end-of-stream reduces syscall rate ~55% and 95p SLO for short requests by ~30ms. Need to validate no regressions for long streaming chunks.

kai: I'll schedule two concurrent canaries: A) manifest fix to re-enable coalesce for vec kernels on 10% hosts, B) proxy write-buffering on separate 10% cohort. We'll compare.

deploy-bot: canary A started: kernel-manifest-coalesce=true on group canary-net-1 (10%).

deploy-bot: canary B started: proxy-buffer-1kb on group canary-net-2 (10%).

lin: add a control group too for the original rollout so we can baseline.

jessica: will do. timeline: monitor 30m for syscall/writev metrics and 1h for 95p tail. If either canary improves and no regression for large requests, roll to 50% then stable.

omar: one more note: watch kvcache hot_shard counters. coalescing might change access timing and introduce microbursts to certain shards. Add shard-level heatmap.

kai: done. also auditing kernel-picker rules now to ensure IO-shape heuristics exist.

jessica: thanks all. i'll post results in channel in ~45m. :eyes:
